claims.text: Increasing aluminum content promotes in situ formation of an alumina-based passivation layer during high-temperature exposure.
The resulting alumina-based passivation layer is continuous and stable.
An alumina-based passivation layer improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
An alumina-based passivation layer improves corrosion resistance.
Increasing aluminum content can preserve mechanical strength while improving oxidation and corrosion resistance.
Increasing aluminum content does not impose a significant density penalty and allows the alloy to remain lightweight.
Lattice distortions arising from multiple principal elements mediate formation of a coherent, continuous alumina or mixed-oxide layer.
The aluminum-enriched alloy forms an adherent alumina scale during high-temperature exposure.
The adherent alumina scale retards further oxidation.
Lattice distortions from multiple constituent elements maintain a homogeneous microstructure.
The homogeneous microstructure supports mechanical strength.
Relative to the lower-aluminum baseline, the aluminum-enriched alloy will exhibit improved high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Relative to the lower-aluminum baseline, the aluminum-enriched alloy will exhibit improved corrosion resistance.
Relative to the lower-aluminum baseline, the aluminum-enriched alloy will show no significant degradation in mechanical strength.
At sufficiently high operating temperature, the protective oxide scale may spall and invalidate the proposed benefit.
Excessive aluminum content may induce brittle intermetallic phase formation.
Brittle intermetallic phase formation compromises mechanical integrity.
